mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods where FEDFUNDS declines by more than 0.25 percentage points over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where UNRATE rises by more than 0.2pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) and monthly industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, which triggers a sell-off in equities, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where both GDPC1 and INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and rising), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods meeting the tightening cycle condition.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months signals robust labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods where PAYEMS increases by more than 100k over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 5% signals weakening demand in the housing sector, which reduces overall economic activity and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where HOUST declines by more than 5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals an overheating economy, prompting aggressive monetary tightening by the Fed, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In the late-cycle expansion phase (characterized by a declining INDPRO and low unemployment), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to impending economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where INDPRO declines and UNRATE < 4.0%.
